newsitem.title: USA: BASEBALL-ORIOLES SET SEASON HOME RUN RECORD IN WIN OVER TIGERS.
newsitem.headline: BASEBALL-ORIOLES SET SEASON HOME RUN RECORD IN WIN OVER TIGERS.

text.p: The Baltimore Orioles clubbed five more home runs, including two by Cal Ripken and a grand slam by Bobby Bonilla, to set a major-league record for homers in a season in a 16-6 rout Sunday of the Detroit Tigers.

The Orioles, whose three-game sweep of the unmenacing Tigers moved them within 2 1/2 games of the New York Yankees in the American League East, boosted their homer total to 243 -- three more than the celebrated 1961 New York Yankees.
"It's just the kind of team we've got, we've got a lot of professional hitters in our lineup and if you make a mistake these guys will hit it," Orioles manager Davey Johnson said.
Brady Anderson (46 homers) led off the game with a homer for the 10th time this season and Ripken added a three-run shot in the first off starter Todd Van Poppel (3-7).
Back-up catcher Mark Parent's three-run blast in the third off Van Poppel was the record-breaker.
The three-run homer gave Ripken 1,358 career RBI, moving him past Brooks Robinson for the all-time Baltimore lead.

"The Orioles have such a rich history of baseball that you have to be really productive over a period of time to get that many RBI," said Ripken said. "I've never been in a lineup that can score runs as prolifically as this one."
Bonilla cracked his fifth career grand slam in the eighth and his 28th of the year, and Ripken followed with his second homer of the contest and 23rd of the season.
In winning for the ninth time in 11 games, Baltimore moved 2 1/2 games ahead of Chicago for the wild card playoff berth.
Tony Clark homered twice for Detroit, who have allowed a major-league record 234 home runs this season.
In Toronto, Woody Williams gave up five hits over eight innings and Joe Carter homered and drove in two runs as the Toronto Blue Jays beat New York 3-1 to end the Yankees' five-game winning streak.
Williams (4-3) allowed one run, walked one and struck out eight as the Blue Jays won for just the fifth time in 15 games. Mike Timlin worked the ninth for his 26th save.
Ramiro Mendoza (3-5) allowed three runs and seven hits over five innings in his first start since July 15.
"We were outpitched today," New York manager Joe Torre said. "Williams threw a great game."
In Boston, Troy O'Leary singled home Lee Tinsley with two outs in the bottom of the ninth as the Red Sox overcame three homers by Frank Thomas to beat the Chicago White Sox 9-8.
Relief ace Roberto Hernandez (6-4) struck out Reggie Jefferson to open the ninth and got Mo Vaughn, who had homered twice, to fly out before Mike Greenwell singled.

Tinsley ran for Greenwell and was singled to second by John Valentin, who also hit two homers. O'Leary followed with a single to centre and Tinsley beat the throw from Darren Lewis to score the winning run.
Thomas hit solo homers his first three trips to the plate to increase his total to 35. Vaughn's pair gave him 40.
Heathcliff Slocumb (4-5), the Red Sox's fifth pitcher, allowed one hit in 1 1/3 innings for the win as Chicago fell 2 1/2 games behind Baltimore in the wild card race.
"We have a knack for making these games pretty exciting," said Boston manager Kevin Kennedy.

In Cleveland, Kenny Lofton's throwing error in the top of the 10th inning allowed Geronimo Berroa to score as the Oakland Athletics snapped a four-game skid with a 10-9 victory over the Cleveland Indians.
The Indians had a six-game win streak halted in front of a crowd of 42,226 fans that pushed them past the three million mark in attendance for the first time in franchise history.

In Minnesota, Salomon Torres tossed a two-hitter for his first career shutout and Ken Griffey Junior, Mark Whiten and Jay Buhner homered to power the Seattle Mariners to their fourth straight win, 7-0 over the Minnesota Twins.
The 24-year-old Torres (2-2) walked two, struck out nine and lowered his ERA from 7.20 to 5.29.
Griffey tied a career high with his 45th homer off starter Rich Robertson (7-15) that sparked a four-run fourth.
The Twins Paul Molitor was 0-for-3 and remains two hits shy of 3,000.

At Texas, Mark McLemore and Mickey Tettleton both homered in the sixth inning and Darren Oliver notched his third straight victory as the Texas Rangers stopped their four-game losing skid with a 6-2 win over the Milwaukee Brewers.
The Rangers, who remained six games ahead of the Seattle Mariners atop the American League West, retired pitcher Nolan Ryan's number 34 in a ceremony before the game.
Oliver (13-6) allowed two runs and nine hits in seven innings. Ed Vosberg struck out two in 1 1/3 perfect innings of relief for his eighth save.
In Kansas City, the Royals' game against the California Angels was rained out.
